topology_reasoning.description: Two parallel waveguides with S-shaped curves for evanescent field coupling
key_knobs: width_um: waveguide core width (0.5-2.0 um range, affects mode confinement)
gap_um: gap between guides, primary coupling tuning knob (0.3-1.5 um)
taper_depth_um: depth of S-curve inward sag (0.1-0.5 um)
length_um: total interaction length (constraint: 18 um fixed by footprint)

iterations.change_made: Initial arc model too narrow. Need larger width, gap. Arc radius causes extended geometry.
Larger width and gap help. But large radius creates 200+ um geometry. Need smaller radius or different model.
Switched to straight rectangles: best baseline. Revealed that width/gap values are correct; now need curvature.
iterations.insight: Target has S-shaped curves, not straight guides. Guides narrow at center where they approach.

iterations.change_made: Added S-shaped taper using faceted polygon (3 control points per edge). BEST RESULT.

notes: Device reached convergence at iteration 4 with IoU=0.593 (exceeds 0.50 target). Straight waveguide model with S-curve taper (sinusoidal sag) matches the target coupler geometry well. All three parametric knobs (width, gap, taper) are top-level tunables that directly control geometry—verified by manual inspection. No gf.Path objects used; purely primitives (rectangles and polygons).
